tickets.actual_outcome: The config lead simply reset the user's (Nik Dainsberg) password, which got them logged in — a routine password reset.
tickets.notes: The investigator couldn't identify the user and produced a broad speculative assessment; the "check account / password reset" direction was reasonable, but the analysis added little value versus the trivial password-reset fix.

tickets.title: HUB - Unable to Reorder
tickets.conclusion: Concluded job 4167985 is blocked from self-service reorder because it is itself already a reorder (reorder_original_id set), and the HUB intentionally blocks reorders-of-reorders; recommended CSR assistance.
tickets.actual_outcome: The agent reproduced it, but the config lead gave the real reason — on Feb 13 the job's material had been changed to a special admin-only material ("z_...MAGNUM RECYCLED MAGNET"), and jobs with admin-only special materials can't be reordered via the button. The customer accepted the explanation.
tickets.notes: Correct that the block is intentional, but the specific mechanism was wrong — the actual blocker was the admin-only special material, not the reorder-of-a-reorder lineage the investigator emphasized.

tickets.title: HUB Order 2083830 - Integration Issue?
tickets.conclusion: Confirmed the order exists in Collaterate but its 5 items were never processed into Pace (production_status null, no Step Functions execution, empty intake queue, no DLQ traces); assessed the ORDER_CREATED event was likely never published/silently dropped; recommended manually triggering the Pace integration and checking the monolith's publish logs.
tickets.actual_outcome: Ticket still open — the agent replied "Checking" with no resolution yet at last update.
tickets.notes: Thorough, evidence-based integration diagnosis internally consistent with all gathered signals; the specific root cause and outcome remain unverified since the ticket had no resolution at capture time.

tickets.title: Printing packing slips from shipments page on producer is not working.
tickets.conclusion: Packing-slip printing from the Producer 2 shipments page was broken because the monolith's `GET /packingSlipPdfByShipmentId/{id}` endpoint returned a non-PDF response (Lambda relay throws 502 `legacy_bad_response`). It attributed this to a known engineering issue tied to the PDF Generator decommission project (TEM-10135) and a prior security remediation.
tickets.actual_outcome: The developer found the real cause was a WAF allow-list outage (Sep 30 18:35 – Oct 1 08:43 CDT) after an InfrastructureLegacy CDK deploy emptied the trusted-IP list, so the printable pages returned a CloudFront 403. Re-running the IP sync fixed it and the requester confirmed. The requester reported it again on Oct 5, support said it was a known issue and then resolved it the same morning, and the requester acknowledged.
tickets.notes: The AI traced the right request chain (Producer 2 → monolith PDF endpoint) but blamed a decommission/remediation project instead of the WAF block, so the stated root cause was wrong.

tickets.title: Delta Print Portal - unable to un-assign a pick and pack fee
tickets.conclusion: Most pick-and-pack fees on the Delta Print Portal (site 194) had already been cleared in the database that morning, but 28 shared-offering rows in `system_offering_site_shares` still carried a fee and were the likely reason the fee still showed. It could not reproduce or explain why the products-page wheel would not un-assign the fee and recommended a dev data fix plus a bug ticket.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer identified a code bug: the `ProductV2Provider` bulk patch always looks up the fee group, so a null (clear) value fails with "pick and pack fee could not be found". The developer also corrected that the 28 remaining share rows are all retired products and need no data fix. The code fix was approved on Oct 21.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly flagged the UI inability to clear the fee as a bug needing a ticket, but its leading explanation (the 28 shared rows) was a red herring and it missed the null-handling root cause.

tickets.title: Kohler Professional Channel - orders cannot be marked as shipped
tickets.conclusion: The error is accurate: each order still has unshipped jobs with no rows in `order_shipment_item_allocations`, so `canStatusBeShipped()` correctly refuses the change. It judged this a data problem on the orders rather than a code bug.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support and dev found the orders contained hidden child product-set sub-jobs (created roughly Jul 7–21, 2026) saved as not visible to admins, so the admin could not mark them shipped. A DB fix was assigned after the triage call and the ticket was resolved on Oct 7, with about ten other orders affected.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly called it a data problem on the orders (fixed by DB update) but did not identify the hidden/invisible sub-jobs or the wider set of affected orders.

tickets.title: Norton Sku 101453310-0001
tickets.conclusion: Actual (0) and Backordered (0) were correct, but Reserved was -7, which made Available show 7. It traced the -7 to a warehouse pick on 2026-09-17 that released reserved units never recorded as reserved, and recommended setting `reserved_inventory` to 0 on variant 78864.
tickets.actual_outcome: The support agent adjusted the inventory and sent a screenshot of the corrected quantities. The requester replied "Thank you!" and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The recommended fix matched what the team did; the requester's expected quantities (all 0) agree with the AI's target values.

tickets.title: Collaterate Reporting is showing stock allocation for a large job that has printed Job # 4701745
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm the root cause. It suggested the 26,000-sheet allocation was an open planned-material line on a matching Pace job (L2077289) with nothing pulled, possibly counted by Redash report 713. It also noted the Collaterate order item was not shipped and still in `production_status_id = 4`.
tickets.actual_outcome: The data engineer found the job's Collaterate production status was never advanced after printing (still "Queued For Print"), and report 713 counts jobs in that state as not yet printed. Production changed the status to printed and the requester confirmed it was fixed.
tickets.notes: The primary Pace-planned-material theory was wrong, but the AI's last recommendation to check the Collaterate production status on the order item pointed at the real cause.

tickets.title: Collaterate communication bug fix - Chat setting return to default
tickets.conclusion: The activity-log filter is deliberately persisted in browser `localStorage` (key `showActivityOptions`, shared by the legacy JSP page and the React order-details UI), so it carries over between orders by design. A follow-up comment found the change already tracked as TTI-24196 and noted it scopes out the legacy JSP page.
tickets.actual_outcome: The team linked the ticket to TTI-24196 and assigned it to Jon Heer; the ticket remained open. No fix had been delivered or confirmed by the end of the ticket's activity.
tickets.notes: Nobody explicitly confirmed the cause, but the team's linking to TTI-24196 matches the AI's finding that this is existing sticky-filter behavior needing a story rather than a defect.

tickets.title: MOD SITES - Homepage feature Menu- category images are now gone- due aSAP
tickets.conclusion: It could not see the screenshot and could not confirm a cause, but the evidence suggested the category-image move from EFS to S3 was only partly rolled out in prod: prod S3 nearly empty, no CloudFront route for `/resources/category_images/*`, and no prod copy recorded. It recommended running the copy, adding the CloudFront behavior, or rolling back.
tickets.actual_outcome: The support agent first saw the images displaying on the affected sites, and within about fifteen minutes the requester said it "appears to have been fixed". No team member stated a cause or what was changed.
tickets.notes: No root cause was confirmed; the hedged EFS-to-S3 migration hypothesis is plausible (a prod S3 object had been written about 20 minutes before the ticket) but unverified.

tickets.title: Fairview MY Products update
tickets.conclusion: It could not find the "Fairview White EPVC - CMYK (First Surface)" product in the prod database. It explained the acrylic product's "Color Note" box comes from the offering's special-instructions headline and recommended setting that headline (and the job-ticket display flag) on the EPVC offering.
tickets.actual_outcome: The support agent found the product was hidden, and the config team (after clarification) added the field by changing the "Color Critical - please indicate job # below" operation to "Allow User to Change This Operation". The ticket was then closed.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly framed it as a config change but could not locate the product and proposed a different mechanism (special-instructions headline) than the one the team used.

tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm a cause but argued the data showed no account-specific bug or server-side error. It concluded the dead Post button and reversed message order point to a front-end/browser problem, and recommended engineering reproduce it and check the console and network tab.
tickets.actual_outcome: The developer could not reproduce it in staging, and support asked the requester to log out and back in to Collaterate. The requester confirmed the issue was fixed. The AI's own later comment on ticket 86970 ties these Oct 2 symptoms (reversed activity log, 403 on posting) to the server-side REST Admin Pilot role regression (TTI-24213).
tickets.notes: The AI concluded there was no server-side error and no account-specific problem, but the symptom was a per-user server-side role rollout (403s), fixed by re-login; its front-end guess missed that.

tickets.title: Collerate Proof files are spinning - Widespread.
tickets.conclusion: It could not find a root cause: proof records looked normal, the instant-proof ECS service was healthy and no proof-related alarms fired. It noted a 5-hour gap in new proof records and recommended checking the proof viewer/download path and S3/CDN permissions.
tickets.actual_outcome: The developer reproduced that both proof and customer print files spun on the order page, and support told the requester to log out and back in. The same fix was used for the activity-log problem reported the same morning (ticket 86952), and the ticket was resolved.
tickets.notes: The AI was honest that it found no cause, but its leads (S3/CDN permissions, upload gap) did not match the session-related fix; same Oct 2 REST Admin Pilot role regression cluster as 86952, 86956, 86960, 86963, 86970.

tickets.title: unable to mark a planned shipment as shipped
tickets.conclusion: It could not find the root cause and said so. The "Save does nothing" symptom matched a known silent-failure pattern in the new Shipments UI (TTI-24155), so a rejected 4xx on the PATCH could be swallowed by the UI, but it had no evidence this was the blocker. It asked for order numbers and a DevTools network capture.
tickets.actual_outcome: The requester added that the general notes section was missing and a shipment showed "site is in demo mode", though she was on the live site and everything worked earlier that morning. Support asked for cache clear and re-login; the ticket closed about two hours later with no stated resolution.
tickets.notes: No cause was confirmed on this ticket; it matches the Oct 2 REST Admin Pilot role cluster (all started that morning, same "demo mode" 403 symptom), which the AI did not connect here.

tickets.title: Unable to Edit Collaterate Addresses
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm a root cause. It judged the missing State and Zip rows in the legacy "Edit Ship To Address" dialog most likely a front-end or payload problem (country flags `hasRegions`/`hasPostalCodes` absent), since the countries table was correct. It recommended a Jira bug, a hard refresh and a support-side address correction.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support asked the requester to log out and back in, which did not help. A developer then said it "should be resolved now" and asked for a cache clear, after which the requester confirmed it works. The requester had also reported a ship error.
tickets.notes: The AI's payload-gap guess and hard-refresh advice were in the right area but it missed the server-side rollout fix; part of the Oct 2 REST Admin Pilot cluster.

tickets.title: Collaterate - 'Post Action' button issue
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm a root cause, but code review showed the "Post Action" button disables itself and is only re-enabled in the server callback. It concluded the problem was most likely a client-side JavaScript error in the internal-action form and found no server-side error.
tickets.actual_outcome: The requester added that the notification log was in reverse order and files were spinning. Support replied only to log out and back in, which is the fix used for all the other Oct 2 tickets.
tickets.notes: Nobody explicitly confirmed a cause here, but the AI's "no server-side error, client-side JS" call conflicts with the pilot-role 403s later documented in TTI-24213/24216.

tickets.title: Text Issue - Cards in The Hub
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine the cause because the description was cut off and the screenshot was not visible, so the repeated "Application" text was unknown. It guessed duplicated option-label data and asked for a screenshot, the exact text and the product name.
tickets.actual_outcome: A support agent replied about an hour and a half later that the issue was resolved and asked the requester to log out and back in. No cause or product was named and the ticket closed.
tickets.notes: The AI was honest about the missing information, but its data-issue guess did not match a resolution that came from a platform fix plus re-login.

tickets.title: Collaterate not processing normal on my end.
tickets.conclusion: It identified this as very likely the known REST Admin Pilot role regression (TTI-24213): reversed activity-log order, 403s on activity-log posts and lost PP Assigned saves all fit, and it is not the user's Mac or browser. It recommended linking to TTI-24213, un-enrolling the user from the pilot role and re-login.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support told the requester and her team to log out and back in, and said that would fix it. The ticket closed about 40 minutes later.
tickets.notes: The only investigator comment of the cluster that named the pilot-role rollout; the team's re-login fix is consistent with that, though no one stated the cause on the ticket.

tickets.title: Can't log anything in Collaterate
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm a system-wide failure, since the Activity Log was writing about 10,000 entries a day and staff and customers were posting normally. It suspected something specific to this user (account, permissions or front-end) and asked for details and a role check.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support said the issue was resolved and asked her to log out and in, but she reported it still failed. Support then asked for a cache clear and a developer tested for her in test-b and found no issue. The ticket was closed on Oct 6 after an unanswered follow-up.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly pointed to a per-user cause rather than an outage and flagged role/permissions; it did not tie it to the pilot-role rollout and no final confirmation appeared.

tickets.title: Collaterate "demo mode"
tickets.conclusion: It concluded the "demo mode" message is a site-level setting and that the Crocs site was in demo mode when the user tried to ship, though the site is now live (updated 2026-09-29), so retrying should work. It admitted it could not prove the timing.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support told the requester to log out and back in, saying that would fix it. No flag change or other cause was mentioned and the ticket closed within an hour.
tickets.notes: The "retry now" advice effectively matched the fix, but the site flag was last changed Sep 29, so the demo-mode explanation looks wrong; the same "demo mode" error appears in ticket 86956 on the same morning.

tickets.title: Collaterate Activity Log - Order Information is backwards
tickets.conclusion: It said the most likely cause was the REST Admin Pilot rollout (TTI-24216): the REST Order Detail path shows the log oldest-first while the classic page shows newest-first, which explains why only some users see it. It recommended linking to TTI-24216, sorting newest-first, or un-enrolling the pilot batch.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support replied within a minute that the issue was resolved and asked the requester to log out and back in. The ticket closed the same day.
tickets.notes: The resolution (mitigation applied, then re-login) fits the AI's pilot-role diagnosis, although support did not state the cause.

tickets.title: Collaterate won't let me add another shipment
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine why Add Shipment from the Distribution Center failed to load, and found no matching error or bug. It judged it specific to the Distribution Center destination (configuration, data or UI code), not an outage or a browser/session problem.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support replied that the issue had been resolved and asked her to log out and in. The requester confirmed it was working again.
tickets.notes: The AI explicitly ruled out a session problem and pointed at destination configuration, but the fix was a platform-side resolution plus re-login (the Oct 2 pilot-role cluster).

tickets.title: Print Points Balance
tickets.conclusion: It found a 440-point gap between the storefront (-4,854) and Loyalty Admin (-4,414) and traced it to a stale PENDING -440 redemption (coupon UiR2yfd5) dated 2025-10-31, probably counted by one view and not the other. It attributed the negative balance to clawback adjustments and recommended cancelling the stale redemption.
tickets.actual_outcome: A support agent's internal note reached the same conclusion, naming the same stale PENDING redemption as the entire 440 gap, and added the decisive -50,762 admin adjustment on 2026-08-27. It was assigned to the loyalty developer and still open with a follow-up on Oct 6.
tickets.notes: The team's analysis mirrors the AI's, though no adjustment or customer confirmation is recorded.

tickets.title: Integration Issues for Job 2080195
tickets.conclusion: It found no system fault: Pace integration checks and queues were clean and the order log had no errors. It said the Part 4 and Part 10 holds kept returning because the condition behind them was not cleared, and guessed Part 17's "no preflight laser" message came from entering the path under the "file path" category instead of "preflight laser".
tickets.actual_outcome: The ERP administrator triggered a resync, and Pace staff found a scheduling problem (start date later than end date on the job plans). They unscheduled and rescheduled the job, integration then succeeded, and the repeating holds were due to the same problem. The requester thanked them.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly called it a Pace data/workflow condition rather than an outage and explained why the holds recurred, but it did not find the schedule-date cause and its Part 17 explanation was not confirmed.

tickets.title: Collaterate Admin Bugs
tickets.conclusion: The symptoms (new Menus UI for only some CIMs, Users page not saving, State/Zip missing in the shipment address dialog) matched the REST Admin Pilot role incident TTI-24216. It noted the bulk role batch had already been removed in prod and recommended signing out and back in to retest.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support said the issue should be resolved and asked for log out, log in and cache clear. The requester did so and confirmed everything that had been wrong was fixed.
tickets.notes: The AI's identification of the pilot rollout and its log-out/log-in recommendation matched the successful fix; it correctly flagged the Users-page link as inferred.

tickets.title: Cannot open tickets on network.
tickets.conclusion: The 403 on the sessionless `printableWorkTicket` URL was a CloudFront/WAF block, because the requester's IP was probably not on the printables allow-list rule (`BlockPrintablesOutsideAllowedIps`). It could not confirm this because it could not read the IP set or sampled requests, and recommended checking the requester's IP and recent IP-set changes.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support called it a known issue being worked with the team and asked whether the user was remote or on VPN. The user was on site on a work computer; later the team said "please try now" and the requester confirmed the tickets open again.
tickets.notes: The team did not state the cause on this ticket, but the fix timing and handling match the WAF allow-list explanation, which was confirmed as the root cause of the earlier Sept 30–Oct 1 outage on ticket 86876.

tickets.title: Pace Tickets not opening
tickets.conclusion: The 403 was almost certainly a CloudFront WAF block, since the rule limiting the printable work-ticket URL to TBG IPs was rejecting requests. It suspected a recent IP-set change (a CloudFormation `UpdateIPSet` at 2026-10-04 23:52 UTC) and could not read the IP set or block logs to confirm.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support called it a known issue and suggested the VPN, which the requester said did not apply because she was in the office. About three and a half hours later the team said "please try now" and the requester confirmed Pace tickets open again.
tickets.notes: The cause was not stated on the ticket, but it is the same incident as 87007, 87015, 87016 and 87009, and the AI's WAF/IP-set diagnosis fits.

tickets.title: Access the job ticket through collaterate since the WSR won't launch the ticket
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine why the WSR (Work Station Report) would not launch the job ticket and had no root cause; its searches turned up nothing on "WSR". It suggested opening the ticket directly in Collaterate as a workaround, getting a screenshot and testing on VPN.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support called it a known issue, got a screenshot over chat, and later said it was resolved and to try again, then closed the ticket. This was the same Oct 5 work-ticket 403 incident as 87007, 87010 and 87016.
tickets.notes: The AI gave no diagnosis and did not link this to the other same-morning 403 tickets, although its Collaterate-lookup workaround was valid.

tickets.title: printing icon not working , not responding
tickets.conclusion: It could not find a root cause. Pace logs showed no print errors, so it judged the problem most likely on the workstation, printer or Producer client side, and recommended testing on the affected PC and checking for a common cause such as a driver or PDF viewer change.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support said it was a known issue the team was working on, and later told the requester to try again. The requester confirmed printing worked, with no workstation change reported.
tickets.notes: The fix was server-side (same Oct 5 printable-page block as 87007, 87010 and 87016), so the AI's workstation/printer theory was wrong.

tickets.title: unable to print out of collaterate
tickets.conclusion: The "error finding your label printer" message is raised in the browser when it cannot reach the local Zebra Browser Print agent or find a default Zebra printer. It said this is a workstation problem and not a Collaterate server fault, and gave steps to check the agent and printer.
tickets.actual_outcome: The requester wrote that it started printing again on its own ("disregard") but that this seems to be happening a lot lately, then agreed to close the ticket. No cause was identified by the team.
tickets.notes: Nobody confirmed a cause; the AI's code-based explanation of what triggers that exact message is sound, and the intermittent self-recovery is consistent with a local agent issue.

tickets.title: Toolkit Inventory adjustment
tickets.conclusion: It could not find SKU 101873753-0001 (product P2036425) in any database it could query, so it could not confirm why Available showed -34 against 52 inventory. It suggested stale or over-reserved quantities and recommended checking the ledger and releasing stale reservations.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found 37 backorders on the SKU and about 51 actual inventory. The requester then said he had worked with the inventory team, the numbers add up now, nothing needs adjusting, and closed the ticket.
tickets.notes: The AI never located the record, and its stale-reservation guess missed that backorders drove the negative Available.

tickets.title: Can't access work tickets through pace
tickets.conclusion: The likely cause was the WAF/CloudFront printables IP allow-list added as a compensating control for a security issue (TTI-23044 / TTI-23060), blocking work-ticket URLs for users whose IP is not allow-listed. It noted Pace backend errors were zero, so the 403 was returned at the edge, and warned that the helpdesk "resolved" note had no verified fix behind it.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support first called it a known issue, then said it was resolved and to try now, and closed the ticket about 20 minutes later. The team did not say what was changed.
tickets.notes: The cause was never stated on the ticket, but it is the same Oct 5 incident as 87007 and 87010; the AI's edge-block conclusion fits and it correctly questioned the unverified closure.

tickets.title: Remove Product Type: "TBG Dye Sub Monti" from the HUB- Christi Chapin
tickets.conclusion: It could not find a "TBG Dye Sub Monti" product type in Collaterate or Redshift, and concluded the HUB product type list is a Pace setting that a Pace admin must remove. It added that nothing in Collaterate needed changing, and suggested deactivating rather than deleting.
tickets.actual_outcome: The configuration team replied a week later that the product had been retired and hidden from The Hub, and the ticket closed.
tickets.notes: The right action (retire rather than delete) matched, but the AI could not find the product and wrongly said the change belonged in Pace rather than Collaterate/Hub configuration.

tickets.title: LIFEWISE Skus showing incorrect backorders
tickets.conclusion: The two order lines (jobs 4680773 and 4718021) were still flagged backordered although stock now existed, because `order_items.stock_backorder_quantity` is a snapshot taken at order time that the WMS inventory sync never clears on open items. It recommended resetting both lines to 0, reconciling the SKU-level backorder count of 1, and checking other Lifewise lines.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support asked a developer to remove the backorder status on the two orders. The developer ran an inventory drift update for the site (9 products had drift) and noted a Java bug that could have caused it was being worked on. The requester thanked them.
tickets.notes: The drift update confirms the AI's "stale backorder not reconciled after replenishment" finding, and the developer's mention of a known bug is consistent with its call for a sync fix.

tickets.title: Matching Envelope operation items share cost tables with envelope press sheets
tickets.conclusion: The database matched the ticket: three active items and three inactive ones (47/48/49) in operation 9 share cost tables with press sheets. It also found six additional inactive items sharing tables and proposed a transactional script giving each operation item its own cost-table copy, leaving the press sheets untouched.
tickets.actual_outcome: The developer created separate cost tables for each item in staging, the requester verified it, and the change was then applied in prod. The developer reported that 14 cost tables shared with press sheets were now split.
tickets.notes: The fix the team applied was the approach the AI recommended, and its extra findings align with the broader count of 14 tables.

tickets.title: Unable to log into Collaterate - New Hire Mark Kadadah
tickets.conclusion: It found no Collaterate account for Mark Kadadah in prod and concluded he could not log in because his account was never created. It recommended confirming the name spelling, creating the user if missing, and checking onboarding provisioning.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support asked the requester to try again, then after the new hire still failed to log in a support agent supplied the default password and confirmed they could log in that morning. The ticket was then resolved without stating whether an account had been created.
tickets.notes: The reply with a default password and "I was able to log in" implies an account was created or fixed after the AI's check, which fits its "account missing" conclusion, but the team never said so explicitly.

tickets.title: Invitations and Cards - misleading header
tickets.conclusion: It could not find where the "Mailing" heading comes from and saw it as a copy/label change request. It inferred from a knowledge-base prompt that the section is probably the matching-envelope option group, said the prod DB had no matching option-group table, and recommended re-filing as a Jira request.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer found the label comes from the `operation_groups` table (id 30, "SF Smartpress Mailing", label "Mailing") created by a 4.44 migration. The same group holds both envelope and real mailing operations, so a simple rename would affect other products and separate groups were recommended. Support later reported it resolved.
tickets.notes: The AI's inference that the section is the envelope option group was right and its rename-to-"Envelopes" suggestion was close, but it claimed no matching DB table exists and missed the shared-group complication.

tickets.title: HUB Tape Application Selection (Finishing) - Christi Chapin
tickets.conclusion: This is a product-configuration request, not an outage. It located the PM Ordering Portal tape-application operations (e.g. "LF Film Tape Application" operations 176–178), pointed to earlier tape changes (TEM-3854, TTI-16704) as models, and recommended reclassifying it as a service request and confirming PID 33157 exists in Pace.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support forwarded the ticket to the configuration lead and left it open (status Open) as of the last update. No outcome or resolution was recorded.
tickets.notes: Nobody confirmed anything, so this rates the analysis only: the classification as a config request routed to the right team is sound, but how a tape PID links to the operations was unconfirmed.

tickets.title: 2087628 - Locatoin unable to update
tickets.conclusion: It could not find why the location change fails for jobs 4730902 and 4730905, found no errors for either job and could not read their state. It noted an unrelated message in the UpdateJobLocation dead-letter queue and said a Pace or Collaterate developer needed to review.
tickets.actual_outcome: The team reproduced it in staging and a developer showed it is by design: a job in Large Format Distro (group id 9) cannot be moved to any other production group, a rule from TTI-347 in 2021. The requester said the products were quoted incorrectly, a new quote was requested, and the ticket could be closed.
tickets.notes: The AI gave no diagnosis and its DLQ finding was a red herring; the real explanation was a coded business rule it did not find.

tickets.title: 2087660 un-cancel job
tickets.conclusion: Job 4730970 is cancelled and the order is already Shipped (changed by the requester minutes earlier). It could not see the exact error but judged the app does not appear to allow un-cancelling a job on a shipped order, so it probably needed a developer or DBA to fix the data.
tickets.actual_outcome: A support agent reproduced it in staging and confirmed the order being in Shipped status is why the un-cancel fails. Changing the order back to an active status let the item be un-cancelled, and the requester was told to do that.
tickets.notes: The AI identified the Shipped-status blocker but overreached in suggesting a data fix when reverting the order status was enough.

tickets.title: Errors for new shipments/partial credits
tickets.conclusion: Its first comment could not identify the cause of the add-shipment, un-cancel and partial-credit errors; transaction, shipment creation and Pace looked healthy and the exception was only in application logs. A later AI comment gave the root cause: the REST Admin Pilot role added to 138 admins on 2026-10-06, whose credit endpoint needs a permission most PCs lack (403) and whose shipment endpoint rejects a facility already on the order. The pilot was switched off and a permanent fix (TTI-24321) raised.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support could not reproduce it in staging, then noted the requester lacked the Accounting permission. The requester later said a developer had identified and corrected the issue, and support closed the ticket the same day.
tickets.notes: The later root-cause comment matches the team's fix (turning off the pilot); the first comment alone had no diagnosis. Same Oct 6 pilot regression as the Oct 2 cluster.

tickets.title: Can't log into Jitbit, password reset link expired/already used
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm a cause with its tools. It suggested an email security scanner opening the single-use reset link first, an older-token mix-up or a username typo, and recommended a Jitbit admin check the account and set a temporary password.
tickets.actual_outcome: A Jitbit administrator said they fixed the login and the requester confirmed it worked; the ticket closed the same day. No cause was stated.
tickets.notes: The recommended admin-side account fix was what resolved it, but the scanner theory was never confirmed.

tickets.title: Braille Hot folder update
tickets.conclusion: The facility-number size is not a hot-folder setting but a hard-coded constant, `ROOM_NUM_FONT_SIZE = 29.3`, in the `mhealthBrailleSetup` handler in `pa-webhook-workers`. It needs a code change to 24 and a deploy, and it should be routed to development.
tickets.actual_outcome: The configuration team agreed, noting that "based on the AI investigator" it is not config related, and handed it to a developer. The ticket remains open and is marked deleted in Freshservice, with no fix recorded.
tickets.notes: The team routed the ticket on the AI's finding; the fix itself was not confirmed.

tickets.title: Custom Quote Items Missing
tickets.conclusion: Its first comment found two of the quote's three jobs gone from the database and could not say what removed them. A second AI comment, posted with engineering help, found the root cause: a bug let the custom quote's project appear as the customer's shopping cart, so the customer's "Remove" clicks on 2026-09-29 permanently deleted 7 jobs.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support told the sales rep this was a system bug, the quote had to be re-created, and a fix was going out the following Wednesday; other quotes were found to be affected. The ticket was closed on Oct 29 with "the issue has been fixed".
tickets.notes: The team's explanation (a system bug, fix pending) matches the second comment's root cause; the first comment alone had no diagnosis.

tickets.title: Lifewise Order 2069816 - cannot cancel part?
tickets.conclusion: It could not identify the cancel error but found job 4680773 still carried a stale backorder quantity set at order intake, while the SKU's backorder had since been recalculated, and a replacement job existed. It tied the stale flag to the failure to cancel.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced it in staging and a developer explained the cancel fails because it tries to release a backorder that no longer exists on the variant after the drift update. The configuration developer ran SQL to clear the stale `stock_backorder_quantity`, and support asked the requester to try again.
tickets.notes: The AI's stale-backorder finding is exactly what the developers fixed; it did not name the release-of-missing-backorder mechanism.

tickets.title: Meta user unable to checkout - PR is the country
tickets.conclusion: The saved address had postal code 987 instead of 00987, so FedEx returned no valid shipping service and the checkout showed "Selected an incorrect shipping service". It said the blank State field is not the cause for Puerto Rico but can block saving the address in stage, and recommended correcting the ZIP and making State optional for PR.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support had already identified the ZIP issue and asked for 00987; the requester corrected the address, noted checkout still asked for a state, and asked to close the ticket.
tickets.notes: The AI comment arrived after support had reached the same answer, and its observation about the lingering State requirement matched the requester's last comment.

tickets.title: Trouble with aText blurbs in Collaterate
tickets.conclusion: It found no server-side cause and hypothesised a client-side conflict between the aText app and the Collaterate browser windows (lost accessibility permission, a rich-text field swallowing keystrokes, or the expansion mode). It recommended checking the user's Mac and the field affected.
tickets.actual_outcome: IT confirmed aText was installed and permissioned correctly and the failures were in the proof status and comments windows after prod release 4.45.2. Developers reproduced it on a Mac with aText but not on Windows, and told the requester it is not a Collaterate issue and happens only with aText on Mac. On Oct 15, however, a linked Jira on the proof-status area was put on hold because the planned new AOD page would cover it.
tickets.notes: The client-side aText theory matches the Mac-only reproduction, but the linked Jira suggests the Collaterate window is also involved, and IT first suspected a Collaterate change.

tickets.title: Not able to upload screenshot to customer account's
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine the cause because the ticket lacked the error text and location; the account looked normal and no logs matched. It guessed an unsupported file type or oversize file, based on an unrelated Instant Proof error, and asked for the error and file details.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support could not reproduce the upload in prod, but in staging reproduced the error and found it went away once the "User & Division Manager" administrator permission was added to the requester. The requester then confirmed "Now it works!" on Oct 8.
tickets.notes: The cause was a permission, not file type; the AI's file-type guess was explicitly speculative and wrong, and it did not suggest checking the requester's role.

tickets.title: CoreMedia- client not getting emails
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm why the user was not receiving CoreMedia (DALIM ES) emails, since the cause sits inside that application. It agreed with routing to the CoreMedia owner and recommended checking the DALIM outgoing mail log and, if messages were sent, the client's spam filter.
tickets.actual_outcome: The CoreMedia owner found ES was handing mail to the TBG mail server correctly but TBG's server was not delivering mail from the @smartpress.com sender, and proposed changing the sender. The requester then reported the client found the problem on Fairview's own end, and the ticket closed.
tickets.notes: The AI's "if sent, check the client's spam filter" branch matched the final cause, but its analysis contained no diagnosis and the sender-domain issue was found by a human.

tickets.title: Can't see some internal order notes
tickets.conclusion: It said this did not look like a permissions problem and the more likely cause was that the requester and her teammate were on different order screens, since only the requester had the REST Admin Pilot role (new `sls-admin-order-details` screen). It could not confirm which note was meant and recommended opening the classic view.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support checked and found the teammate also had the REST Admin Pilot role, contradicting the AI's premise, and could see the notes when logged in as the requester. The requester then restarted her computer, could see the notes, and confirmed.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly ruled out permissions, but its different-screens theory was disproved and the real fix was a client-side restart.

tickets.title: Override is not available in collaterate today - I cannot plan jobs
tickets.conclusion: It could not reproduce the missing Override but said the best lead was the requester being on the REST Admin Pilot version of Order Detail, which has known gaps, and recommended removing the user from the pilot role or toggling the feature flag.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support confirmed the requester held the REST Admin Pilot role, then logged in as her and saw the Override. The requester said it was working again and asked to close the ticket; no cause was stated.
tickets.notes: The pilot-role lead was confirmed (the user held the role), but no one confirmed it was the cause of the missing Override.

tickets.title: Re: Collaterate Dev Request - Layout Adjustment - Save and Cancel Buttons Covered by Notification/Error Bar
tickets.conclusion: It said no technical investigation was needed because the ticket was only a "Looks good, thank you!" confirmation reply to an earlier dev request. It recommended closing it and linking it to the original request.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support replied that it was a response to ticket 86675 and closed the ticket.
tickets.notes: The AI did not find the original ticket number but the handling matched its recommendation exactly.

tickets.title: Shipping cost accurate?
tickets.conclusion: The $33.73 FedEx Home Delivery rate looked consistent with how Collaterate priced earlier shipments to the same rural Maine ZIP ($33.01–$33.12) and showed no calculation error. It suggested counter pickup as an alternative and that any dispute over the markup is a rate-adjustment setting, not a bug.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reviewed prior orders and found shipments to that ZIP consistently charged $33.12 or $33.01, and the requester accepted the answer and asked to close the ticket.
tickets.notes: Support's finding matched the AI's price comparison.

tickets.title: Issue with color on reorder being changed to Black ink only
tickets.conclusion: The reorder picked up a new "Matching Envelope Printing Ink Type" operation (created Dec 2025) that the original 2024 order never had, and it defaulted that operation to the first item, "Black Only". It saw this as a data and default-value problem rather than an outage, inferred from comparing the two jobs' operations.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support first could not reproduce it, then reproduced it in prod and stage. A developer confirmed the AI investigation was correct and the configuration team set "Full Color" as the default for that operation on the Cards PJC. Support also gave a manual workaround for the pending job.
tickets.notes: The fix, changing the operation's default, is exactly what the AI's analysis pointed to.

tickets.title: Split shipment not available in activity log? Order 2089844
tickets.conclusion: The second shipment was added manually on 2026-10-07 10:33 UTC by a named user, not created by the Sephora import, and nothing was written to the activity log when it was created, which is why the requester could not see it there.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support relayed the AI finding, and a developer confirmed from the code that neither the classic admin shipping screen nor the newer shipment API writes an activity-log entry when a shipment is added. The requester said that told her what she needed and the ticket could close.
tickets.notes: Code review matched the AI's data-based conclusion.

tickets.title: Character Limit for "I Will Describe Delivery Method" Shipping?
tickets.conclusion: No 64-character limit exists today: the text lands in `order_shipments.shipping_service_notes`, a `text` column, with no validation, and about 10% of recent shipments (1,663 of 17,053) exceed 64 characters. It recommended a TTI ticket adding both UI maxlength and server-side validation.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer proposed exactly that UI plus server-side limit with no database change. After clarification from the requester and the warehouse team, they confirmed they would enforce 64 characters on all sites and leave existing orders unchanged.
tickets.notes: The ticket remained open for the implementation, but the agreed approach matches the AI's recommendation.

tickets.title: Producer PID 22782 needed
tickets.conclusion: It could not find a cause. PID 22782 is active in Pace with stock on hand and not in the Collaterate material specification table, so it was likely excluded from the New Gang picker because it is sheet stock while the picker offers roll stock. It said this was unconfirmed and a dev should check how the picker builds the material list.
tickets.actual_outcome: The configuration team lead replied the same day that the requester was "all set" and the requester confirmed the PID is now there. The fix was not described.
tickets.notes: The outcome shows a configuration change, which fits the AI's pointer to product material mapping, but the sheet-versus-roll theory was not verified.

tickets.title: Storefront closing out and shipping jobs
tickets.conclusion: It did not find the root cause and could not verify the line-item statuses. It found that the manual per-line "Ship" action sends an email by design (`sendNotificationEmail` is hardcoded true), so the duplicate emails are expected, and suggested developers check whether shipping the job still cascades "Shipped" to line items.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found the example order was a BOM Builder order and linked it to ticket 86869 (hidden sub-jobs preventing shipped status). It was passed to the developers; by Oct 23 a list of non-shippable orders had been produced for review, the requester confirmed the KOHLER Professional Channel shipments on it could be shipped, and the lines were being marked shipped manually while developers explored longer-term improvements. The ticket was still open.
tickets.notes: Nobody confirmed the cause; the AI's by-design email finding looks valid but it missed that this is a BOM Builder / hidden-sub-job order like 86869.

tickets.title: Fix for current printing
tickets.conclusion: Collaterate already had job 4741628 set to 2-sided, but the edit was made after the job went to production, so D2P likely still carried the original single-sided setup. It recommended re-triggering the job update to Pace/D2P and re-releasing the job.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer reached the same conclusion: the job changed to 2-sided at 8:14 AM CT but the print file had been requested at 7:08 AM CT, and production was told to re-request the print file. On Oct 15 support added that D2P's default retry had used the stale notification, a fresh print-file request would pull current data, and a Jitbit ticket should be raised if it recurs. The reporter said a new D2P error appeared on Oct 13, and no final confirmation was recorded.
tickets.notes: The diagnosis matched; the follow-up D2P error afterward was a separate unresolved problem.

tickets.title: Sticker Pricing on Smartpress Website Down
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine why Instant Quote was unavailable on Custom Die-Cut Stickers and found no outage or error. Its strongest lead was that the product had been updated about 18 hours earlier by a named e-commerce user, so it recommended asking them what changed and checking pricing inputs.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced a "pricing engine could not be reached" error and passed the AI's suggestion to the e-commerce team member. Support said it was resolved about 40 minutes after the ticket opened and the requester thanked them; the fix was not described.
tickets.notes: The AI's change-on-Oct-8 lead was the one the team acted on, but the actual cause and fix were never recorded.

tickets.title: Collaterate notifications
tickets.conclusion: The requester already has access to Collaterate Notifications and it found no permission gap. It guessed she wanted to see her teammates' notifications and said no role setting for notifications was found.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support tested in staging and found the Notifications view only worked after the "Internal Notifications" role was added. The configuration team added that role in prod.
tickets.notes: The AI explicitly concluded there was no permission gap and that no permission table controls notifications, when a missing role was the whole problem.

tickets.title: 2027 Saddle Stitch Calendar IDML Layout Guides Need Adjustment
tickets.conclusion: The 2027 IDML files were present in S3 and look intact, but were uploaded without a Content-Type, which would make a browser treat them as unknown files. It recommended re-uploading the seven files with Content-Type `application/octet-stream`, and said it could not check the layout guides.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support suggested a Safari download setting or Chrome, and the requester could not open an IDML to check. A support agent noted the 2027 Layout Guide URL points to an `.idml` file and that changing it to `.pdf` opened the file. On Oct 13 the requester reported the customer said the initial browser troubleshooting had resolved the problems, and the ticket closed.
tickets.notes: The browser-handling-of-an-unrecognized-file theory is consistent with the browser troubleshooting that fixed it, but the Content-Type cause was never confirmed.

tickets.title: Re: Turn off PID 8311
tickets.conclusion: No investigation was needed: the ticket is just an email reply ("Thanks all!") to the "Turn off PID 8311" thread, with no incident or request. It recommended closing it as a follow-up to ticket 87245 and handling any remaining work there.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support noted before the AI comment that it is a response to ticket 87245 and closed it.
tickets.notes: The AI comment was posted after the closing note and repeated the same conclusion, adding stock-flag details from the thread.

tickets.title: Auto-follow PM Outsourcing
tickets.conclusion: This is a feature request, not an incident: the behaviour does not exist, and it can be added in the order-created handler (`event-handler-order-created.js` in `sls-event-handler`) by inserting active `order_item_followers` rows after the PC is assigned. It suggested a per-assignment-group flag and noted orders that already have a CSR are skipped.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support delivered a checkbox for each PC Assignment Group in the Event Handler app, "Auto-follow matching jobs", disabled by default. The requester thanked them and the ticket was closed on Oct 29.
tickets.notes: The shipped design is the per-group flag the AI recommended.

tickets.title: CQ history: when copying, add item to history in both quotes
tickets.conclusion: This is a feature request. `CustomQuotesRepository.createQuote` writes the "Duplicate Quote" history entry only into the new quote, and the fix is to load the source quote after duplicating and append a matching entry to it, with a test and a TTI story.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced it in staging, then a developer made a quick fix the same day so the original quote's history shows the number of the quote it was duplicated into. The ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The change made is the one the AI described.

tickets.title: Delta Print Portal SKU 101899829-0001 adjustment
tickets.conclusion: Actual (33) already matched, but Reserved was 0 (expected 2) and Backordered was 8 (expected 0), after a warehouse pick event and a "true up" earlier that day. It recommended a developer correct the variant to reserved 2, backordered 0, with an adjustment row for audit.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support adjusted the inventory and posted a screenshot, and the requester thanked them. The ticket closed within about ten minutes.
tickets.notes: The expected final values the AI stated match what was set.

tickets.title: add a sales rep filter to the PC queue
tickets.conclusion: This is a feature request, not an incident. The PC queue (`sls-pc-queue`) has no sales-rep field or filter, there is no existing Jira work, and it recommended a TTI story covering the queue payload, filter parameter and UI control.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support confirmed only the PC filter exists in the queue, and the requester supplied the queue link. The ticket is still open with no delivery recorded.
tickets.notes: Nothing contradicted the AI's finding and no fix was confirmed.

tickets.title: Facebook Pixel
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine why the Facebook catalog shows only 4 products. It found the theme sends only a hard-coded Purchase event without product IDs and said the cause may be missing or mismatched `content_ids`, with the Pixel and catalog settings sitting in Meta and GTM that it could not read.
tickets.actual_outcome: Engineering fixed the pixel on Oct 15 so it sends product IDs in the format Meta's catalog expects. The catalog still held few products because Meta's catalog crawler was being blocked by site security, which engineers asked to allow; the requester accepted the update and the ticket stayed open.
tickets.notes: The ID-format theory matched the first fix, but the AI missed the crawler block that kept the catalog small.

tickets.title: Collaterate JitBit access issues
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm the cause because its tools cannot see JitBit. It thought the one-time reset links were most likely being consumed by an email security scanner, and listed an inactive or locked account as another possibility, recommending a JitBit admin check the account.
tickets.actual_outcome: The JitBit administrator explained that a licensing change to per-technician fees deactivated accounts that had not been used recently. They reactivated her account as a standard user, and she logged in and filed a ticket.
tickets.notes: The AI's top theory (link scanner) was wrong, but its recommendation to have an admin check the account's active status found the real cause.

tickets.title: No front lam required for Printed Summa cut jobs - UV Roll Product Type - Christi Chapin
tickets.conclusion: It could not make the change or tell which Hub product the ticket meant. It showed front laminate is controlled per print job classification (`show_front_laminate`) and listed the UV Roll and Summa classifications that currently show it, recommending the configuration owner turn it off for the correct one.
tickets.actual_outcome: The configuration lead is assigned but no reply or resolution was posted; the ticket remains open.
tickets.notes: Nobody confirmed anything, so the rating reflects the analysis: the mechanism is correct and Hub-config-based, but the specific classification was not identified.

tickets.title: Collaterate Log Out Issue
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm the cause. It found the same @smartpress.com address exists as both a staff login and storefront customer accounts, a plausible source of session conflicts during assisted sales, and said it had no evidence of any domain-based logout logic.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer found the reporter's @smartpress.com email was attached to other Smartpress customer accounts and that her staff username used that domain instead of the usual TBG address, and logs showed her session being destroyed. The email was removed from the other accounts and the ticket was kept open to watch for recurrence.
tickets.notes: The AI's hypothesis of an email shared between staff and customer records matched what the team found, though whether it fully fixed the logouts was not yet confirmed.

tickets.title: Lifewise sku 100778143-0001 adjustment
tickets.conclusion: The variant showed Actual 14, Reserved 14 and Backordered 14, and the 14 backordered units came from one of two items on order 2089801 flagged backordered even though stock was on hand. It recommended zeroing the variant backorder and correcting the order item.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer adjusted the backorder on the product page, and the configuration developer made the order-level correction. The requester then realised the customer had put 28 of the same part on the order across two jobs, so one job (4735596) was cancelled and the SKU adjusted.
tickets.notes: The data fix the AI described was what was done, but it treated the backorder as a false flag when it came from duplicate quantities on the order.

tickets.title: Jitbit #105187021
tickets.conclusion: It could not identify the order or the cause. The ticket named no order and the cited Jitbit tickets were unreachable, so it asked for the order number, page and error text.
tickets.actual_outcome: The requester explained that new Jitbit alerts keep saying the proof file has the wrong number of pages although it matches the Collaterate ticket, and tied it to ticket 87334 (the D2P stale-data issue). The ticket was still open at the last update.
tickets.notes: The AI offered no diagnosis and did not connect the alert to the same-week D2P/print-file request issue in 87334.

tickets.title: Assisted Sale - Order Placed Notification, No Order
tickets.conclusion: Inconclusive: the ticket did not identify the custom quote, so it could not trace it. It found no errors in the quote-update Lambda, said a silent missed status update was possible, and noted the custom-quotes service had been deployed the day before (PRs #156 and #158) as an unreviewed timing coincidence.
tickets.actual_outcome: The developer found a race condition: the customer ordered from a stale quote page while the admin had the quote in Requote and clicked "Submit to Customer" two seconds later, which overwrote the Ordered status without checking. The developer corrected the quote's data (Ordered and linked to the order) and planned two guards; the ticket closed on Oct 29.
tickets.notes: The AI's suspected missed status update was a symptom, but it offered no cause and its deploy-timing lead was not the cause. Its manual-fix workaround matched the data fix applied.

tickets.title: Sephora 2.0 ID 27032-UBF not triggering backorder
tickets.conclusion: The backorder was not being persisted: the variant's counters were stuck at 0 even though 46 open items for 47 units existed, and the variant was last updated by `anonymous` eight seconds after the new job was created. It judged this a defect or data drift, recommended running the inventory reconciliation script and avoiding cancel-and-re-add.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support adjusted the backorder to 1, but re-adding the job did not trigger it, so the configuration developer made a further fix ("all set"). The job then showed as Backordered and the requester confirmed.
tickets.notes: The counter-drift finding was borne out by the manual adjustments needed, though the AI's suggested root cause (the sync resetting values) and the reconciliation script were not confirmed.

tickets.title: Collaterate order total calculating incorrectly 2091274
tickets.conclusion: The line items correctly sum to $7,231.74, but the order header holds an older $6,870.15, which is what is charged. It said the header was probably not recalculated after the 10/14 job-price edits and admitted it could not explain exactly how the header reached $6,870.15.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support first blamed a Requote bug, then retracted that. The final finding was that Requote works as designed (it only flags a price adjustment), the jobs are priced correctly, and the header was lower because the 5% Nonprofit discount was applied a second time at checkout on 10/07, a custom-quote handling bug partly fixed on 10/14.
tickets.notes: The AI's observation of the $361.59 header gap was accurate, but its stale-header explanation was wrong; the double-applied discount was the cause.

tickets.title: Unable to adjust shipping speed
tickets.conclusion: It could not find the cause. The order data showed her teammate Karl's change from Direct Mail Services to FedEx Home Delivery succeeded, and nothing pointed to a problem with the order. It recommended comparing the two users' roles, capturing the network response and escalating if it recurs.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support compared roles and tried it in staging with her credentials, where the change worked. The requester noted her screen showed FedEx Ground instead of Home Delivery, and support confirmed the Home Delivery option was not visible for her. The ticket was closed the same day without a stated cause.
tickets.notes: The AI's user-specific lead was right and the role comparison it proposed was done, but it gave no cause; this lines up with the Oct 15 REST Admin Pilot screen gaps (see 87541, 87556, 87562).

tickets.title: Logic needed for Interchangeable Retractable Banners (New SPDC Product)
tickets.conclusion: The operation and choice IDs in the request are valid (operation 10 is Banner Stands; operation 122 is TBG Velcro Application, choice 4329). It agreed with earlier triage that this needs a developer-configured logic rule because the system has no cross-operation rule engine, and suggested splitting the product into two variants as a workaround.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support's first reply called it a feature request, then a developer posted that the logic was now up on Prod. The ticket closed on Oct 29.
tickets.notes: The AI's feature-request classification and ID validation were consistent with the outcome; the method used to implement it was not recorded.

tickets.title: Printing Collaterate packing slips now have blank page
tickets.conclusion: After two earlier comments (a returns-QR block theory that it then retracted), its final comment found the root cause: the packing slip page forces a page break after the slip and the admin layout then adds an empty footer `div`, so Chrome prints a blank second page on every slip. It named the fix (TTI-24713) and a print-dialog workaround.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer confirmed the fix under TTI-24713 for hotfix 4.46.1, support gave the workaround, and the fix went live in prod on Oct 15 with the blank page gone.
tickets.notes: The final AI root cause matched the shipped fix, but the first comment blamed the wrong feature and needed two corrections.

tickets.title: Can't Override/Change Descriptions in Collaterate
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm the root cause. The backend save code for site-share descriptions looked correct, so the fault was probably in the UI request or how a blank description is persisted. It suggested capturing the network call and entering a space as a workaround.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found the problem disappeared in staging when the REST Admin role was removed from the user, and a developer fixed it in release 4.46.1, which went live the same day.
tickets.notes: The AI pointed at the UI request rather than backend code, which fits a REST-pilot-screen defect, but it did not identify the pilot role.

tickets.title: Error occurred. Contact support for help if the problem persists
tickets.conclusion: It could not find the cause: the logs and Sentry showed nothing. It noted two of the four orders were already In Process and the others were in different states, and asked for the exact action, time and username.
tickets.actual_outcome: The requester said the error appears on "Ship It". A developer explained the REST pilot screen was hiding the real refusal reasons (insufficient inventory on 2088513, a FedEx "Shipper Postal-State Mismatch" on 2089015), fixed in hotfix 4.46.1. Support later gave the backorder-split instruction for 2088513 and closed the ticket.
tickets.notes: The AI's observation that two orders were already In Process was right, but it missed the pilot-screen error masking and the individual shipment refusals.

tickets.title: Custom Quote - Cards Dimensions Issue
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm the root cause but concluded custom quote products should not accept open-ended dimensions, so a maximum width and height capped at the press sheet should be enforced server-side. It found no existing Jira or max-size check in the code snippets it saw.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer found the custom quote tool skipped its maximum-size check when "Pieces On Sheet" was overridden (96), so a mistyped 9494" width saved and ordered. The fix, rejecting any size larger than the press sheet even with the override, is scheduled for the Nov 11 release.
tickets.notes: The AI's recommended server-side size limit matches the fix, but it believed no check existed when the real defect was a bypass of an existing check.

tickets.title: Collarerate Shipping Widget issue
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine the root cause. It found shipment S-2535770 had no shipping vendor or service assigned, which could explain empty rows, and called the problem a UI rendering issue or bad data, recommending a console check, dev review and assigning a vendor and service.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer confirmed it as a REST Admin Pilot issue, reproduced on a test environment, with the classic screen working. It was fixed in 4.46.1, which went live Oct 15, and the shipping options reappeared.
tickets.notes: The AI's "UI rendering" instinct was close, but it pointed to missing vendor/service data on the shipment as the trigger, which was not the cause.

tickets.title: Saddle Stich Booklet Ordering Page
tickets.conclusion: It could not find a root cause: no outage, alarm or matching Sentry error. It read the screenshot as an existing cart item in edit mode, pointed to possible but unconfirmed contributors (the TTI-23994 storefront bootstrap migration and the TTI-24223 cart JavaScript crash), and asked a developer to reproduce it with the browser console open.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support could not reproduce it in prod for the reporter's own account (impersonated, which also holds the REST Admin Pilot role), another user or three customers. After the reporter pushed back, support said on Oct 16 that the issue had been resolved and asked her to log out and back in, and the ticket closed.
tickets.notes: The AI's leads (bootstrap migration, cart JS crash) were not what resolved it; the log-out/log-in fix matches the Oct 15 REST pilot hotfix pattern, but no cause was stated.

tickets.title: Adding Online Special shipping
tickets.conclusion: It could not determine why the option was missing. It ruled out a missing Collaterate carrier service (`system_shipping_services` and `shipping_vendors` had nothing named "Special" or "Online") and said it might be a Pace shipping method or a site-specific shipping option that the configuration team would need to create or enable.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced it in prod and stage: the Special Shipping operation in Production Plan Details offered only three choices, without "Online Special Shipping". The configuration team added it as an option on the product's PJC on Oct 19 and the ticket closed.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly said a configuration change would be needed and ruled out carrier services, but it looked in the wrong place and did not identify the operation choice.

tickets.title: OLF labels not printing when in the gang window
tickets.conclusion: It could not find the cause. It guessed the OLF gang job built by `impose.ts` in `retail-gang-phoenix-api` might not carry the member jobs' label tasks, and recommended getting a gang number and checking logs and Sentry; printing from each individual job works as a workaround.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced it in stage and prod: on the Producer gang page the Labels button shows a raw template or a count of 0 and does nothing, with a console error in `getSelectedJobLabels` because `items` is undefined. It was assigned to a developer and closed as resolved on Oct 20.
tickets.notes: The real fault was in the Producer gang page's front-end label-count code, not in the gang-creation task flattening the AI suspected.

tickets.title: Meta MOD Site - product was allowed to backorder
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm a root cause. The Meta site's `backorder_enabled = false` was correct and no order showed a backorder, but three orders had reserved stock that did not exist, pushing available inventory to -3, which behaves like a backorder though it is not one. It noted the code guard only flags such items rather than blocking checkout.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support could not reproduce it and escalated to the dev team. A developer later found the three single-unit orders were accepted correctly with 16 on hand, then a warehouse cycle count of -16 took on-hand to 0 after the orders were placed, and nobody was alerted. A PR (7800) was in review to alert users and the warehouse team, and the ticket remained open.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly separated this from a true backorder and found available at -3, but it said the reservations had no stock behind them rather than identifying the post-order warehouse cycle count.

tickets.title: Kohler Signature Stores - 11 products 1212305
tickets.conclusion: The most likely cause is that the site 531 product JSP template no longer compiles because the generated method exceeds the JVM's 64KB limit, which would break every product page on that template. It based this on a log excerpt already posted in the ticket and recommended splitting the JSP or reverting the last template or product change, and treated the "visible to segments" setting as unrelated.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer posted that it had been fixed, without describing the change, and support closed the ticket after confirming it was resolved. The log excerpt on the ticket, posted by support before the AI comment, showed the same JSP compile error.
tickets.notes: The fix details were not recorded, but the AI's compile-limit reading of the logged error is the only technical explanation on the ticket.

tickets.title: Sephora Inventory ID 27432 Incorrect reserved quantity?
tickets.conclusion: The reserved quantity of 5 was wrong: it found no active placed order holding stock, and the 5 appeared left over from 8 cancelled order items (cancelled Oct 19) whose `stock_reserved_released_quantity` stayed 0, so no release was written. It recommended resetting `reserved_inventory` to the correct value (likely 0) and filing a bug for cancellations not releasing reservations.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support saw that every order for the SKU had been cancelled, offered to set reserved to 0, and the requester agreed. Reserved inventory was set to 0 and the requester placed the store punchlist order before the deadline.
tickets.notes: The data fix applied is exactly what the AI recommended; the underlying cancellation-release bug was not discussed.

tickets.title: Unable to Allocate
tickets.conclusion: Its first comment found no root cause and suspected a browser-side hang. A second comment, written after support reproduced it in prod, found the root cause: the Allocate panel throws a JavaScript error on orders with customer rework production runs for users in the REST Admin Pilot role, because the REST run DTO omits job and offering names. It named the fix commit under TTI-20177 and the hotfix 4.46.3, with a classic-screen workaround.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the greyed-out Allocate screen in prod on order 2047266 and said the issue was resolved that afternoon. The requester acknowledged and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The second comment's pilot-role diagnosis fits the Oct 19 hotfix cluster; the first comment alone was inconclusive but correctly suspected a client-side hang.

tickets.title: HealthMarkets - Trying to Add Additional information fields on new products and getting error message - due ASAP
tickets.conclusion: Its first comment could not find the cause and noted the "This is a required field" error is a backend validation. A second comment confirmed the root cause: for users in the REST Admin Pilot role, a JSON-parsing change meant drop-down values and Admin Display choices were dropped, so the backend rejected the field. It cited a fix commit under TTI-20177 for hotfix 4.46.3 and a classic-screen workaround.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support escalated to the dev team and reproduced it in staging, then said the issue had been fixed within about seven hours. The requester confirmed it was working and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The final diagnosis matches the confirmed fix; the first comment correctly identified the validation message but not the cause.

tickets.title: Permission to change Sales in Collaterate
tickets.conclusion: It could not identify the exact permission that controls editing the Sales Rep on an order. It treated the request as an access request and recommended a System Admin compare the user's roles with a colleague who can edit the field, grant the missing role, and confirm site access.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support assigned the "Order Sales Rep Manager" role to the requester, verified by logging in as her, and the configuration team confirmed the update. The requester confirmed it worked and a second user was updated the same way.
tickets.notes: The AI did not name the role but its role-comparison-and-grant recommendation is what resolved it.

tickets.title: Date Picker additional info fields won't save the "show on order" checkboxes
tickets.conclusion: Its first comment found the three Date Picker fields saved with an empty `admin_display_options` list, a defect in the Date Picker save path rather than user error. A second comment said it was fixed in 4.46.3: the REST pilot save was dropping the Admin Display choices, the same defect as ticket 87620, and the affected fields need their checkboxes re-set.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support said the issue was resolved and gave the re-save instruction, and the requester confirmed "This is working now" on Oct 20.
tickets.notes: The data finding was correct and the second comment's root cause and re-save instruction matched what the requester did.

tickets.title: Smartpress Site Order Pricing Discrepancy - 2047266
tickets.conclusion: Its first comment confirmed the split (six of eight items saved at $23.08, the item's production cost) but found no root cause. A second comment, posted by the developer using the AI account, found it was bug TT-367: duplicating an item in the cart priced the copy at production cost; the order was placed 2026-08-18 and the fix went live 08-19. The customer was undercharged and the reorder price of $161.47 is correct.
tickets.actual_outcome: The developer told support that the reply above was theirs and that the customer was undercharged because of a bug on the first order. The requester thanked them and the ticket was closed on Oct 29.
tickets.notes: The final explanation is the confirmed answer, but it came from a developer-assisted follow-up; the first AI comment alone could not explain the pattern.

tickets.title: Job Configuration Defaults: side2InkType: 0 is ignored by the new quote engine, so single-sided products quote as 4/4
tickets.conclusion: The code in `sls-pdp-product-configuration` confirmed the reported root cause: `getDefaultId()` treats an explicit 0 as falsy, so `side2InkType: 0` falls through to the PJC's default ink. It recommended checking raw values before calling `getDefaultId`, adding tests, and avoiding ink 6 ("None") as a workaround.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer wrote a matching root-cause analysis (same file and functions, same fix) and asked the platform developers on Oct 23 to implement it in the serverless repo. The ticket was still open.
tickets.notes: The requester's own write-up already contained the cause, and the AI and developer agreed with it; no fix had been delivered yet.

tickets.title: Jobs Not in Producer "Planning" Section
tickets.conclusion: It did not find a definite cause, but both jobs were valid, not cancelled and Production Ready, yet missing from the production queue, and both parent orders were already marked Shipped even though the jobs were not. It hypothesised that this mismatch kept them out of Planning, and recommended resetting the order status through the admin tool rather than placing more reworks.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer advised changing the order status back to In Process, then switching each job's production status to Planning and back to Production Ready to re-sync it in Producer. The requester said "This solution worked!"
tickets.notes: The AI's shipped-order diagnosis and "reopen the order, not more reworks" advice matched the fix.

tickets.title: DQ - unable to set "Ordered As" to EA from Pack SKU102543482
tickets.conclusion: The symptom is real: "Ordered As" is stored as Pack (`PA`) at the system level and the edit does not save. It could not find why, suspected a blank selection being ignored in the admin save path, and suggested a developer set `stock_unit_of_measure` to NULL as a stopgap.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced it in prod and stage, then found it did not happen without the REST Admin Pilot role and that a separate pilot fix was still in progress. A developer updated the field for the SKU as a workaround and the ticket was closed on Oct 21 as fixed.
tickets.notes: The AI's data-level stopgap matched what was done, but it missed that the edit failed only under the REST Admin Pilot screen.

tickets.title: AAP Sku 102276805 not showing backordered
tickets.conclusion: It could not confirm a cause: order line 4749033 had 8 units ordered and 0 backordered while the variant held 5 on hand and 5 reserved, so a shortfall existed that was not recorded. It suggested the warehouse sync overwrites reserved and backorder values, and recommended a developer set `stock_backorder_quantity` and the variant backorder through the application.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer calculated 13 units open across two orders against 5 available, so 8 should be backordered, and asked the configuration developer to adjust prod. He replied "you are all set" on Oct 22 and the requester thanked him.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly found the unrecorded shortfall and recommended a data fix, but its warehouse-sync theory was not confirmed and the team computed the backorder across both open orders.

tickets.title: Turnaround time shows “undefined Max Quantity” on new master product
tickets.conclusion: The AI saw DB `max_qty=0` for master product 109465 and could not reproduce the issue. It suggested the value was probably missing at first and filled in by a later save.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer reproduced the issue in staging and traced it to the REST Admin Pilot role (TTI-24894). It was fixed and the ticket was closed Oct 21.
tickets.notes: The AI did not identify the pilot-role root cause and offered a "stale value" explanation instead.

tickets.title: Lucid - Variant cannot be disabled
tickets.conclusion: The AI found `enabled=true` still set on the variants and called it a product bug in the disable DELETE path (`removeSiteOfferingVariant`).
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer reproduced the issue and tied it to the REST Admin Pilot role. It was fixed with PR 7779 and closed Oct 21.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly identified a product defect but not the pilot-role cause.

tickets.title: Fjallraven MOD - Approval in Site Settings error
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not reproduce the error or confirm a cause, and asked for the exact error text.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer reproduced the error only with the REST Admin Pilot role and fixed it in PR 7780. The ticket was closed Oct 21.
tickets.notes: No root cause was offered. This is part of the second pilot cluster.

tickets.title: Customer Login Not Working - Julie Jacobsen
