tickets.conclusion: The AI found a curly apostrophe (’) in the stored username while a straight apostrophe was being typed.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support confirmed the same cause and gave the copy/paste workaround. The customer logged in and the ticket was closed Oct 22.
tickets.notes: Correct and specific diagnosis.

tickets.title: MOD Sites - Links to Category Pages now say NULL
tickets.conclusion: The AI identified a known REST-pilot display bug (TTI-24530, PR #7784) that was not yet in prod.
tickets.actual_outcome: The issue was reproduced with the pilot role and fixed in hotfix 4.46.5 on Oct 21. The requester confirmed.
tickets.notes: The AI tied the issue to the right known defect.

tickets.title: True Commery Foundry
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not find why Kohler never received an EHDI for the three orders, and it could not see the True Commerce side. It confirmed that the orders were approved in Collaterate on 9/30 (not 10/1) with blank PO fields and no outbound EDI log entries. It recommended checking the True Commerce Integration Service and the editools owner.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found that the orders were approved before the configurator's "BOM builder" had completed. The fix was to move the orders from In Process to On Hold and back to In Process, which re-triggers the EDI 850. The requester acknowledged.
tickets.notes: The AI's Collaterate-side facts were correct (approved, no PO, no EDI send logged). It did not find the BOM-builder timing root cause, and its True Commerce investigation steps were not what resolved it.

tickets.title: Collaterate Customer Name Business Classification Update
tickets.conclusion: The AI explained the existing rules-based business/personal classification. No rule uses star rating, and the personal-email-domain rule can override a business name. It found that 11 five-star customers are classified personal, all through the email-domain rule. It said this needs a development change and recommended a star-rating rule, reordering the rules and changing the default.
tickets.actual_outcome: An engineer confirmed the rules live in the monolith but the auto-classification engine runs in a separate process. The engineer also agreed the ask is a broader rework (default to business, reprioritize rules, add star rating and purchase history). The ticket was escalated to L3 and linked to the existing epic TTI-24056. No fix had been delivered.
tickets.notes: No confirmed outcome yet. The AI's analysis matched the engineer's scoping. The AI did not locate the engine, which it flagged as unverified.

tickets.title: Collaterate issue
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not find the root cause because the ticket had no order number. It suggested a possible link to the recent removal of the Archive action (TTI-24188/TTI-24779), labelled as a hypothesis.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found a permissions problem caused by the REST Admin Pilot role. Removing the role from the user, re-login and cancelling the job worked, and the ticket was closed Oct 21.
tickets.notes: The AI's archive-removal hypothesis was wrong, and it did not suspect the pilot role. It was honest about having no evidence. Part of the second pilot cluster.

tickets.title: Supplier Reference in MOD sites
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not confirm the cause. Its most likely explanation was a missing `SUPPLIER_REFERENCE` edit permission, which makes the code skip the save silently. It confirmed that the value was never stored and that the problem was not platform-wide.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the issue in staging and tied it to the Rest Admin Pilot role. Removing the role let the user save the value, and the requester confirmed the workaround worked. The dev team was working on a permanent fix.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly pointed to a permission-related silent drop of the field, but it missed the pilot role as the trigger.

tickets.title: Bulk Load Stock Products tool doesn’t save Replacement Cost
tickets.conclusion: The AI confirmed the requester's diagnosis in code. The bulk tool sends `replacementCost`, but the create DTO only accepts `stockReplacementCost`, so the value is dropped silently. It recommended renaming or aliasing the field, adding tests, and checking the Expiration Date requirement.
tickets.actual_outcome: The ticket was still open, with the work routed to a developer. No fix was reported in the ticket by the audit date.
tickets.notes: Nobody has confirmed a fix, so this rating reflects the strength of the analysis. It matched the requester's diagnosis and added evidence from other repos.

tickets.title: B1 measurement
tickets.conclusion: The AI found nothing to investigate. The ticket describes itself as a measurement ticket for a reconciler feasibility build with "No action needed", and the notes look like test payloads. It recommended closing the ticket as a test artifact.
tickets.actual_outcome: The ticket was closed (status 5) the same day with no action taken.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly recognized a synthetic test ticket and did not run needless queries.

tickets.title: Error Loading Orders from DC for Team Cogan in Collaterate
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not determine the cause of the generic "Error occurred" banner on the Team Cogan orders page. It found no account, role or permission problem for the new requester. It suggested the new account's lack of orders or division mapping, or a recent error-handling change (TTI-24741), as candidates.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found the order had been placed by another user. A Collaterate order can only be opened by the person who placed it, and the page shows a generic error instead of an access message. The requester accepted the explanation and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly ruled out an account problem. It did not identify the order-ownership restriction. The ticket gave no order number, so the AI could not check ownership.

tickets.title: FedEx Authenticated Delivery
tickets.conclusion: The AI said the platform already supports a direct "signature on delivery" option for FedEx and UPS, but it is disabled on every site. It found no support for FedEx Authenticated Delivery, which would need new development. It recommended enabling the existing option per site and opening a TTI to scope Authenticated Delivery.
tickets.actual_outcome: Engineers confirmed the signature feature is implemented end to end and only needs to be enabled per site. TTI-24829 is a separate bugfix and does not block it. The requester said they want it for Smartpress customers only when requested, and support planned to enable it after a quick test.
tickets.notes: The AI's reading of the code and feature state was borne out. The ticket was still open at the time of the audit.

tickets.title: Laminating estimated times
tickets.conclusion: The AI traced the 1h26m estimate to the formula on operation item 272 (600 s setup plus 3.27 s per press sheet, last edited in 2022). It noted that this implies about 1,100 sheets/hour against the real 250, and that there is no sides multiplier. It recommended confirming real rates and updating the formulas as a data change.
tickets.actual_outcome: The config team updated the laminate time formulas, which apply to new jobs. The requester then corrected the target rates to 4 s per sheet, or 8 s if double-sided, and the config team applied them. The ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The diagnosis and the recommended fix (a data change to the formulas) matched what was done.

tickets.title: Temp Badges
tickets.conclusion: The AI found no record of where badge stock is kept at SPSC. It summarised the temp-badge types and the Genea print steps from Confluence. It recommended bringing blank cards and printing from the SPSC printer.
tickets.actual_outcome: The IT technician offered to bring blank cards and print the badges on Monday, and the requester agreed. The ticket was still open.
tickets.notes: The AI's practical step matched the plan the team settled on. The ticket was an informational request, so there was no root cause to find.

tickets.title: Jira tickets stuck in placing.
tickets.conclusion: The AI found no bug in Collaterate. The orders matched the Auto Order Intake Python (AOIP) behaviour described in the ticket: order 2103720 already existed, and order 2102104 already existed so the ticket was treated as a duplicate. It said the root cause is in AOIP's resend handling, which it could not inspect, and recommended AOIP fixes plus manual ticket moves.
tickets.actual_outcome: The responder said code changes were being made to help with this and to surface when it occurs. The ticket was marked complete, with future work orders handled by the code update.
tickets.notes: The AI's Collaterate-side data supported the requester's explanation, and its recommended AOIP fixes match the direction of the code change. It could not see the Jira SCWO tickets.

tickets.title: 2076433 - Unable to cancel hards proofs or reworks
tickets.conclusion: The AI found the rework saved as cancelled but still holding a shipment allocation (9 of 9 recent child items). It treated this as a likely application bug in the cancel or allocation cleanup and left the root cause unconfirmed. It recommended a TK bug and a manual cleanup of the allocations.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the issue in production and tied it to the REST Admin Pilot role. The cancel saves and Producer shows the job as cancelled, but the order page does not receive the cancelled status for pilot-role users. PR #7815 fixed it for the Oct 28 release.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly established that the cancel itself saved and that it was a product bug rather than user error. It pointed at shipment allocation cleanup rather than the pilot role, and the manual-delete workaround it suggested was not needed.

tickets.title: update PID
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not tell what "PID 4402" refers to. It found offering records matching 4402 and 32874 but could not link them to a requested change. It asked the requester to say which system the PID appears in.
tickets.actual_outcome: The config team said the Aberdeen Soft Knit 4.5oz fabric in Collaterate now points to Pace ID 32874 instead of 4402, and that new jobs pick up the new ID. Existing jobs still show 4402.
tickets.notes: The AI's clarifying questions were reasonable, as the ticket was ambiguous. It did not reach the fabric/Pace ID interpretation, and the offering records it matched were not the relevant ones.

tickets.title: Failure to Call to Press - 4750465-1
tickets.conclusion: The AI found that job 4750465-1 has no ship or finish date in Collaterate (all four date fields NULL). It concluded that the date was never written for this rework and recommended setting the dates manually, as the sibling jobs have them.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support saw the job as Printed and asked the requester to clear the cache. The requester then confirmed it was showing Printed, and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The ticket was resolved as a stale display in the requester's view. The AI's conclusion that the date was missing led to a manual-edit recommendation that was not needed.

tickets.title: Collaterail - permissions
tickets.conclusion: The AI said this is not a bug. The requester's roles on the stage environment were never copied from prod, since her stage admin account has only Order Viewer and no Shipping role. It recommended an admin add the roles in stage and check whether stage resets would wipe them.
tickets.actual_outcome: The config team confirmed the prod roles did not carry over to stage, restored them, and added Shipping in prod. The requester confirmed it looked good, and the team judged it was an accidental adjustment that should survive stage resets.
tickets.notes: The AI's diagnosis and fix matched exactly, and it correctly flagged the stage-refresh risk.

tickets.title: HealthMarkets - New Agent Kit Order 2106217
tickets.conclusion: The AI found no system error. The eight child template jobs had no personalized file (null session code and file URL) while the kit parent job did. It treated the ticket as a manual art-creation request for prepress and suggested the dev team look at why the template output did not generate for the child jobs.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the issue in staging. An engineer explained that nothing in the system personalizes the kit's child CHILI jobs, because the kit answers are stored only on the parent job. A designer was added to build the art manually, and templated print files were then generated for all POD jobs. A developer later said the PDF failure was probably a temporary CHILI problem and that the kit process is a known manual workflow.
tickets.notes: The AI's reading of the data and its recommendation to produce the art manually matched what happened. It did not identify the missing parent-to-child data copy or the CHILI instability.

tickets.title: Collaterate - more oddities
tickets.conclusion: The AI said this is not a display bug. A one-time image-migration job (`MigrateOfferingImageFilesToS3-prod`) wrote its own name into `site_offerings.updated_by` on about 31,900 products, which overwrote the real last editor. It recommended a TTI bug and restoring the values.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the issue in prod. The responder confirmed to the requester that the system job's name shows on about 31,900 products because it moved images and wrote its own name as editor, and that a person did not edit them. The requester accepted this and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The cause, the product count and the explanation to the requester all matched. The restoration of original editor values was not done.

tickets.title: Presbyterian Foundation URL Name Request
tickets.conclusion: The AI found that the site already exists in prod and is not live, and that its `subdomain_prefix` was cut off at 20 characters. The requested prefix is 23 characters. It could not find where the limit is enforced and recommended a developer change or a data fix.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support tried the admin fields and confirmed that Short Name and Subdomain Name both accept only 20 characters. The request stayed open and escalated for a dev change.
tickets.notes: Nobody had resolved the request at the time of the audit. The AI's finding of a 20-character limit, rather than the 22 the requester said, matched support's test.

tickets.title: #2100456 - Packing Task
tickets.conclusion: The AI found no root cause. It called the freeze a client-side or UI problem that it could not reproduce, and it noted that Pace, Sentry and task data showed no related errors. It suggested a hard refresh, a browser console capture and a review of that day's merged PRs.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the issue in staging and tied it to the Rest Admin Role. With that role, the Special Packaging and Special Shipping choices show incorrectly and cannot be saved, while without it they work. The issue was passed to the dev team.
tickets.notes: The AI's pointers to a client-side cause and a recent deploy were wrong, and it missed the pilot-role cause. Part of the second pilot cluster.

tickets.title: No longer a spot to add the cost when doing "I will describe delivery method."
tickets.conclusion: The AI judged this to be a regression in the new order-details UI. It said the actual-cost field is only drawn when the shipment has third-party billing data, which a describe-delivery shipment normally lacks, and that it is not editable after shipping. It recommended a TTI bug.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the missing field, but another order in staging showed the cost field. A developer said the page needed a refresh after changing the shipping service, then found it only affected REST Pilot users. A fix was deployed and the requester was told the issue was fixed.
tickets.notes: The AI correctly identified a UI defect in the cost editor but described it as general behaviour for every describe-delivery shipment. The actual trigger was the REST pilot rollout.

tickets.title: Chili Required Fields Prompt Adjustment Request
tickets.conclusion: The AI confirmed the code behind the request. `validateChiliDocument()` in `personalizeController.js` returns on the first empty required variable, which explains why only one field is reported. It also uses the internal `name` rather than a display name. It outlined a small change and noted the ticket is really an enhancement.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer asked for an example product with multiple required fields and was given the Fairview Appointment Card. The ticket was still open and the change had not been delivered.
tickets.notes: No fix was confirmed, so this rating reflects the strength of the analysis. The requester had already named the same function, and the AI confirmed it in code. The AI flagged that the display-name property name was unverified.

tickets.title: Can't login into JITBIT
tickets.conclusion: The AI found nothing in TBG's infrastructure that explains the issue. It judged Jitbit to be an external SaaS product, so the login and password-reset errors were most likely on the Jitbit side or in the account. It recommended asking for the exact errors and having a Jitbit admin check the account.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support asked the requester to try again, and the requester then confirmed it was fixed. The ticket does not say what was changed.
tickets.notes: The AI's pointer to a Jitbit-side account issue is consistent with a quick fix by support, but the ticket does not confirm the cause. It did not offer a specific root cause.

tickets.title: Meta MOD - stock products sales tax category
tickets.conclusion: The AI did not find the cause. It said the data showed no clear failure and suspected the offering save path changed by TTI-21192 might null `salesTaxCategory`. It recommended that a developer reproduce the problem.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced it in staging. Support said the data is saved in the database and only the UI does not show it, and that removing the Rest Admin Pilot role is a workaround. A fix was deployed and the requester was told on Oct 29 that it was fixed.
tickets.notes: The AI's TTI-21192 suspicion was wrong, and it missed the pilot-role UI cause. The AI also implied values might be lost, while the actual data was saved. Part of the second pilot cluster.

tickets.title: Producer
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not pinpoint the cause because the ticket had no job number, error text or screenshot. It pointed to unrelated Producer back-end sync errors in Sentry (`_cost_obj_exists` and connection resets) and said it could not confirm they caused the problem.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found an "Access Denied" error in the logs for the requester's request to the production workstations endpoint, granted the missing permissions, and asked the requester to log out and back in. The requester confirmed it was working and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The Sentry errors the AI cited were not related, and the true cause was a missing permission. The AI explicitly did not claim a cause. It asked for more detail, as support also did.

tickets.title: https://collaterate.jitbit.com/ - unable to login
tickets.conclusion: The AI said it could not fix this from the available tools. It identified the site as a vendor-hosted Jitbit instance and judged this to be an account or access issue inside Jitbit. It recommended that a Jitbit admin check whether the account was disabled or removed, and reset the password.
tickets.actual_outcome: A support engineer fixed the issue and told the requester she could log in. The ticket gives no details about what was changed.
tickets.notes: The AI's reading that this was a Jitbit account matter was consistent with the outcome, but the cause was not recorded.

tickets.title: 2108296 - Product Template Not Generating
tickets.conclusion: The AI found that job 4783576 has a closed template session but no output file URL, file ID or preview URLs, while the sibling jobs have them. It did not find the root cause. It recommended checking the template vendor session for an output file and re-triggering the callback, or having the customer redo the template.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the issue in prod. The preview opens as a blank document and the file could not be saved. The config team built the PDF manually from the customer's information and sent it to the requester. No root cause was recorded in the ticket.
tickets.notes: The AI's data findings were correct and its "customer supplies data and the file is rebuilt" fallback matches what happened. The root cause remains unknown.

tickets.title: Collaterate - Edit Basic Properties Error
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not identify the cause because the error text was in an unseen screenshot. It guessed that the data saves but the response or the UI handler that closes the popup fails. It recommended getting the error text and checking a possible link to the COMET-to-REST conversion tickets.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer reproduced the problem in prod only and found that the save returned a 4xx "Visibility cannot be changed when product status is not ACTIVE" for shared products. The cause was a reference comparison of `ProductStatus` objects that fails when the status comes back through the Hibernate second-level cache. The fix was in progress and the ticket was closed on Oct 29.
tickets.notes: The AI's observation that the data saves but the response fails was in line with the real behaviour. It did not identify the cause, and its pointers to the COMET-to-REST tickets were not relevant.

tickets.title: Error occurred. Contact support for help if the problem persists
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not determine the root cause of the generic error when voiding a shipment. It found two live UPS shipments on the order. It suspected a UPS-side rejection, such as a label already voided or already scanned, and asked for logs.
tickets.actual_outcome: A developer found the first void succeeded at UPS but the Collaterate transaction rolled back after a Hibernate `StaleStateException` on the inventory variant, caused by a stale second-level cache copy. Every later retry failed because UPS said the shipment was already voided. The developer reproduced it in staging, noted the order needed a database fix, and later reported the issue fixed.
tickets.notes: The AI's "label already voided" hypothesis matched the state seen on the retries, but it did not find the rollback and the stale-cache root cause. The user held the Rest Admin pilot role, but it was not the cause.

tickets.title: adding file for non-profit
tickets.conclusion: The AI found that the requester's admin account has no system roles, while her two teammates have 9–10 roles each. It said this was the likely cause of the failed uploads and recommended granting the same role set. It could not confirm which role the upload needs.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support's logs showed Access Denied errors, and in staging, granting the User & Division Manager role let the image save. The config team updated the requester's credentials and told her to log out and back in.
tickets.notes: The AI identified the missing roles and named User & Division Manager as a candidate, which proved to be correct.

tickets.title: 3rd Party Shipping Issues
tickets.conclusion: The AI said the most likely cause is a code gap when a job is routed to the South Carolina fulfillment center. The new shipment does not copy the reference shipment's third-party billing settings, and it rebuilds billing from the site configuration, so billing falls back to the Smartpress account. It said this was a strong lead and not yet proven.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support reproduced the issue in staging by adding a planned Large Format - SC shipment, which showed the Smartpress billing account instead of the customer's. The developer then reported that the fix was available in production and closed the ticket.
tickets.notes: The AI's cause matched the reproduction. The ticket does not describe the exact code change, so the match rests on the reproduction steps.

tickets.title: 2109185 - can't set dates
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not find the cause of the "can't set dates" problem because the ticket does not say which screen or date field fails. It noted that 2109185 matches both a new order and an old, shipped 2021 job. It found blank ship dates on the new order's shipment, which it said is expected until the order is processed, and no errors in the data sources it could reach.
tickets.actual_outcome: The ticket was still open at the time of the audit, with no human reply recorded and no cause confirmed.
tickets.notes: Nobody has confirmed anything, so this rating reflects the strength of the analysis. It was careful about the ambiguous number and asked the right clarifying questions, but it did not offer a cause.

tickets.title: Window Decals Product Configuration
tickets.conclusion: The AI found the cause in the code. In the removable cling (PJC 678) second-surface branch, the white-stock case sets the ink configuration to "Standard CMYK (Second Surface)", while production wants First Surface on white stock. It recommended changing that line, and checking the static path and which copy of the file is live.
tickets.actual_outcome: The config team said it is not a config issue. A developer posted the same code branch and called the second-surface ink line "the bug", then assigned it to the developer working on related ticket 87970. The ticket was pending with no fix recorded.
tickets.notes: No fix was confirmed yet. The AI's finding agrees with the developer's, and it flagged real uncertainty about which file copy is loaded.

tickets.title: thd services sku 101117985-0001 adjustment
tickets.conclusion: The AI found the SKU on the THD Home Services site with backorder at 20 and recommended setting `backorder_inventory` to 10 for a requested available of -10. It noted the variant is warehouse-managed, so the value could be overwritten.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support adjusted the inventory, but the requester reported that order 2098843 still showed 20 on backorder. A developer then fixed it and found 4 other products on that site with inventory drift. The order showed 10 afterwards.
tickets.notes: The AI's diagnosis of the SKU's current values and the target change was right, but it did not anticipate the extra drift between the variant and the order. Inventory data-fix family.

tickets.title: AAP SKU 102276805-0001 adjustment
tickets.conclusion: The AI confirmed the SKU shows a backorder of 5 although actual inventory is 161 and reserved is 8. It recommended setting `backorder_inventory` to 0 and checking the warehouse sync and open order items.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support adjusted the inventory within about 10 minutes, and the ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The AI's diagnosis and requested change matched. Inventory data-fix family.

tickets.title: Sephora Product ID 27432 Adjustment
tickets.conclusion: The AI could not find an "Inventory ID 27432" on the Sephora: Inventory site and made no change. It found that 27432 matches variants and offerings on other sites, so it recommended asking the requester to confirm the SKU or item name before anyone adjusts stock.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support adjusted the inventory about four minutes after the AI comment, without asking for clarification. The ticket was closed.
tickets.notes: The AI's caution about the ambiguous ID was reasonable, but support identified the correct item immediately, so the AI failed to resolve a routine inventory-adjustment request. The requested quantities were not verified.

tickets.title: Collaterate # 2103629
tickets.conclusion: The AI found job 4790505 on order 2103629, still active with 1 unit on backorder. It could not cancel it because of read-only access, and it recommended that support or an admin cancel the job through the order admin.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found that the job could not be cancelled in prod. In staging, it could be cancelled once the order status was changed to In Process, while the order was in Shipped status. Support told the requester to set the order to In Process and cancel, and the requester confirmed it was fixed.
tickets.notes: The AI's reading of the data was correct, but its "cancel it through the admin" recommendation did not work as written. It missed that the order status blocked the cancel, and a REST Admin pilot comparison was part of the test.

tickets.title: Backorder Issue with Order 2098843
tickets.conclusion: The AI found that job 4760641 shipped only its in-stock quantity of 90 and the 10-unit backorder was still recorded on it. The requester's quantity adjustment moved the units to job 4790709 but never cleared the flag on the already-shipped job. It recommended a data fix setting `stock_backorder_quantity` to 0 on job 4760641.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support adjusted reserved and backorder quantities, but the job still showed as backordered. A developer then ran an UPDATE setting `stock_backorder_quantity = 0` on job 4760641, and the requester was told the backorder status was removed.
tickets.notes: The diagnosis and the data-fix recommendation matched what was done. Inventory/backorder data-fix family, related to #88235.

tickets.title: Some IDs are not being allowed to be ordered in Collaterate
tickets.conclusion: The AI stopped without a root cause. Both SKUs (27432 and 28513) were active, visible and in stock, so it could not tie the ordering failure to the product records. It noted that both had been edited within a minute of each other on Oct 27 by one user, after their last orders, and recommended asking that user what changed.
tickets.actual_outcome: Support found that minimum quantities of 100 and 20 had been set on the two products in prod, which stopped small orders from being added to the cart. A config engineer confirmed the minimums were set by that same user, and after that user changed them the requester confirmed they were fixed.
tickets.notes: The AI's pointer to the Oct 27 edit by that user was the right lead, but it did not check ordering minimums and told the team the products looked correctly set up.
